title: fix(voice-call): keep continue poll deadline on the monotonic clock
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Running `voicecall continue` while the system clock shifts (NTP correction, laptop sleep/resume, manual time change) could make the command overrun its configured poll budget or report a spurious timeout after only ~1s of real polling. The continue-result poll loop now measures its deadline on the monotonic clock so the budget is unaffected by wall-clock jumps.

- Problem: `pollContinueGateway` seeded the poll deadline with `Date.now()` (wall clock) — `deadlineMs = Date.now() + timeoutMs` — then read the remaining budget back with `Date.now()` and fed it to two `setTimeout`-based consumers (the gateway RPC timeout via `callVoiceCallGateway`, and the inter-poll `sleep`). A wall-clock jump between seed and consume makes `remainingMs` diverge: a forward jump sends it negative and breaks the loop early; a backward jump inflates it and lets the poll overrun the budget.
- Solution: Seed and read the deadline with `performance.now()` (monotonic). The seed, both reads, and both `setTimeout` consumers now share one clock domain that cannot be moved by NTP or sleep/resume.
- What changed: `extensions/voice-call/src/cli-gateway-call.ts` — three `Date.now()` calls in `pollContinueGateway` replaced with `performance.now()` (deadline seed, `remainingMs` read, `sleepMs` read). No new helper, branch, or configuration surface. Budget value, clamping, poll interval, `Math.min` bounding, and break/throw behavior are all unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

Mechanical clock-domain alignment: the deadline was already consumed by monotonic `setTimeout` timers, so seeding/reading it on the monotonic clock makes seed, read, and consume consistent. Matches the established pattern in merged sibling PRs (#159555, #155799, #162813, #162779).

- Best fix: the three replacements sit in `pollContinueGateway`, the canonical owner of this deadline. No caller repeats the seed/read, so no guard duplication is needed.
- Alternative rejected: injecting a `monotonicClock` abstraction. `pollContinueGateway` reads the clock directly and `performance.now()` is the language-level monotonic primitive — injection would add a test seam with no production benefit.
- Risk: `performance.now()` returns sub-millisecond floats; both consumers are bare `setTimeout` (the RPC path goes through `clampTimerTimeoutMs`, which floors; `sleep` truncates floats). Neither uses `AbortSignal.timeout` (which would reject floats), so no flooring is required. Consistent with the sibling PRs.

## User Impact

`voicecall continue` now respects the configured poll timeout budget even when the host clock jumps. Operators on laptops that sleep/resume, or hosts under NTP correction, no longer see premature "voicecall continue timed out waiting for gateway operation" errors or silent budget overruns on this path.

## Evidence

**Real behavior proof (unchanged Gateway client)** — the production `pollContinueGateway` owner runs unmodified against the **unchanged** `callGatewayFromCli` / `GatewayClient` WebSocket transport. A minimal loopback WebSocket server speaks the Gateway protocol (connect.challenge → connect → hello-ok → method request/res) and always returns `{status:"pending"}` for `voicecall.continue.result`, so the loop only exits via deadline exhaustion. The real Gateway client is pointed at it via `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL`; no transport binding is replaced. A +300s wall-clock (`Date.now`) jump is injected after the seed; on the fixed code the deadline (`performance.now()`, monotonic) is unaffected, so the poll exhausts the budget and throws a bounded timeout. Pre-fix (`origin/main`), the same jump makes `remainingMs` go negative and the loop breaks at ~0ms.

```console
$ node --import tsx/esm proof-transport.mjs   # head 9f4de26e53d, POST-FIX
=== BUG-173 / PR #164951 transport-boundary proof (head 9f4de26e53d) ===
monotonic budget (ms): 5000
wall-clock jump injected mid-poll (+300s): true
production owner threw bounded timeout: true
elapsed monotonic time (ms): 5001
PASS (deadline stayed on monotonic clock via UNCHANGED Gateway client): true
Observed: the production pollContinueGateway owner, using the UNCHANGED Gateway client
(WebSocket transport via OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_URL), kept polling until the ~5s monotonic
budget exhausted despite a +300s wall-clock jump — the deadline stayed on performance.now.
```

Pre-fix (source reverted to `origin/main`, same harness — the real Gateway client still connects, but the `Date.now`-based deadline breaks immediately):

```console
$ node --import tsx/esm proof-transport.mjs   # PRE-FIX (origin/main)
=== BUG-173 / PR #164951 transport-boundary proof (head 9f4de26e53d) ===
monotonic budget (ms): 5000
wall-clock jump injected mid-poll (+300s): true
production owner threw bounded timeout: true
elapsed monotonic time (ms): 0
PASS (deadline stayed on monotonic clock via UNCHANGED Gateway client): false
FAIL: poll did not respect the monotonic budget under wall-clock jump
```

Observed result: post-fix the poll ran ~5001ms (bounded by the 5s monotonic budget) despite the +300s wall-clock jump; pre-fix it broke at ~0ms (the jump made `remainingMs` negative on the second `Date.now()` read). The deadline stayed on the monotonic clock. Stable across repeated runs.

**Regression test (supplementary, bidirectional)** — `extensions/voice-call/src/cli.test.ts`, 27/27 pass post-fix; pre-fix `expected "vi.fn()" to be called 4 times, but got 3 times` (the jump breaks the loop before the 4th poll).

**What was not tested**: A genuine host NTP correction or sleep/resume end-to-end (the harness injects the wall-clock jump via a `Date.now` override, which is semantically equivalent — it proves the seed/read no longer consult the wall clock). The `setTimeout` internals were not modified; only the budget passed into them changed clock domain.

**Open PR collision check**: PR #159510 modifies the same file but only touches `isGatewayUnavailableForLocalFallback` / `hasConfiguredRemoteGatewayTarget` — orthogonal to clock/deadline/polling. No collision.

**Changed test cost**: `extensions/voice-call/src/cli.test.ts` — 27 tests, single-worker vitest run reports `Duration 11.84s` (real wall time ~28.5s including vitest startup/transform; `tests` slice 2%, `transform` 51%, `import` 36%). The shard runs in the `checks-node` CI job whose `timeout-minutes` budget is 20 (hosted runner). Net test lines +54 across this one file; no new test file or shard.

## AI Assistance

A coding agent assisted with analysis and implementation under human direction. Per review, added a real-behavior proof that exercises the production `pollContinueGateway` owner with the unchanged Gateway client (WebSocket transport) under an injected wall-clock jump, replacing the earlier loopback-transport demonstration, and added the changed-test-cost measurement.
